text:
William Nylander is in the middle of Toronto's worst stretch, and the trade talk has found him. Hockey Patrol and Markerzone both ran stories this week on him answering trade rumors, and The Hockey News quoted him on the breakdown behind Minnesota's winner: "Something We Have To Sort Out". The Maple Leafs have lost six straight.

His season line still looks like Nylander: 11 goals and 22 points in 22 games. The recent part doesn't. He's pointless in four straight, and the chances have thinned out with it (2.9 expected goals on his own shots over his last ten, against 3.5 usual). His 11 goals came on 8.0 expected, so the early finishing was carrying him even before the slide.

The deeper concern is five on five, where Toronto gets only 41.1% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 8 points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey flagged the defensive cost last season too (bottom 6% of forwards). What to watch: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 60% of his shots coming off the rush. When Toronto stops winning pucks back, Nylander stops getting his best looks.
headline: Nylander's slump, Toronto's losing streak and the rumors
